personas.why: Gym-going techie; the ghost overlay stops the scroll and the 14-vs-11 self-own is fun, but the 'AI judge vs AI coach vs tool' layering loses him before the payoff. Might send it to a gym friend.
The red/green ghost earns 3 s and the skeleton dots are neat, but the twist refers to a reel he never saw and he can't tell which AI is which. No stake for him.
Holds through the dots and the knee graph because they are pretty. Leaves when it becomes a creator arguing with his own tools; she doesn't yet know what went wrong in the set.
The hook image is intriguing but 'a pose tool pins seventeen dots' signals a tech explainer. At 10 pm, with no human stake yet, he scrolls.
Not a gym or AI person. The opening legend text is confusing and the first line promises nothing she wants.
Exactly his project-idea content: pose estimation, knee angle to rep count, honest failure modes. Watches to the end and saves the diagram; may comment GHOST.
Likes the graph-from-body moment, but beat 6 is a pile of numbers (14, 11, 11°, three margin notes) with the payoff still 15 s away.
Respects the honesty, but at 19 s he has heard three caveats and seen no result. Too much process.
Interested in AI and gym, and the visuals are slick. The middle feels like a methodology slide; he may skip ahead and miss the ghost payoff.
Appreciates 'my best set, not a textbook' as an idea but never reaches it. The twist and error beats delay the insight.
Admires the hook craft and the loop, and the self-deprecating count error is likeable. He can see the retention dip in beats 5–7 and wouldn't save a pipeline diagram.
Strong opening image, but there is no clear single message; it reads as an in-joke for followers of the series.
The guardrail that says 'can't see your knee' instead of guessing is the detail he loves. Saves the diagram and would comment for the safety-check rules.
Occlusion failure, tracker jump and blind agreement check are all credible and rarely admitted. Watches fully and likely comments, possibly a nitpick about 2D angles from one camera.
The ghost-over-bad-set is the most relevant visual for him and he wants to see the form fault. He gets 20+ s of dots, graphs and AI errors first, and the fault arrives at 37 s.
The cool overlay holds 3 s, then it turns explainer-ish. No personality or story beat early enough to keep a casual 20-year-old.

strongest_beat: 1 (and its return in 9–10): two bodies in one frame with the red gap is instantly readable and loop-worthy
weakest_beat: 5: the twist depends on a previous reel, introduces a second AI ('coach') beside the tool and the judge, and undercuts the premise before the payoff has been shown
top_fixes: Bring the payoff forward: show the caught set, the named fault and the stamp by about 12–15 s, then explain how it works. Mass and finance viewers currently leave at beats 5–6, 20 s before the answer at 37 s.

Cut one thread. Pose tool, AI coach, Fable judge, safety check and blind tally are too many actors for 46 s; move the 'STOP stamp vs AI coach' twist and the blind-check tally to the caption, and keep only the 14-vs-11 fail as the honesty beat.

Make the hook carry a human stake. Use the regret line ('I should never have done this set') and replace the legend text 'GREEN = MY BEST SET · RED = THIS ONE' with plain words such as 'AI FOUND MY WORST SET'; a legend is not a reason to stay.

Simplify beat 6 to one joke: 'it counted 14 reps, I did 11'. Drop the 11° reading and the three margin notes; move the hidden-leg explanation into beat 7 as a single visual, and use 'my AI' instead of 'pose tool' and 'rep maths' in speech.

Make the ending pay off for non-builders: state the fault in gym words a trainer would use, with a real consequence, and close on 'which lift should I ghost next?' or 'send this to your gym partner'. 'The whole system in one drawing' and a pipeline diagram are a save asset for builders only. The reel also depends entirely on the unfilled judge slots; if the real fault is mild, rework the premise.
